A real photograph, a still frame from a live-action commercial shot on a large-format 65mm digital cinema camera. EXACTLY ONE PERSON in frame.

A wide shot of a quiet city park. Just left of centre, about 9 metres from camera, an older man sits alone on a weathered wooden park bench with black cast-iron arms, both feet on the ground and his hands resting on his thighs, facing the camera. A tree trunk rises near each top corner, and their leafy branches hang into the top of the frame. Behind the bench, about 30 metres back, is a long, uneven line of mature oaks and plane trees, with a lamp post and the low roofline of distant brick buildings showing between them.

Seen from standing eye height, the camera level and square to the bench. 60mm lens, natural compression, straight lines, the man sharp and the tree line behind him softly out of focus.

The man is the one in the reference image: same face, grey stubble, flat grey tweed cap, navy wool peacoat, brown trousers and brown leather shoes.

The ground in front of the bench is a worn asphalt path with patched cracks, fallen leaves and a painted kerb edge, which gives way to slightly uneven grass with bare patches near the bench legs. The bench slats are grey-brown, with peeling varnish and a few carved scratches. There's a green metal bin beside the bench.

Light: low autumn afternoon sun from camera left, raking across the path. It throws long soft shadows from the bench and the man to the right and puts a warm edge on his cap and shoulder. The tree line behind falls into cool shade. The sky is a soft, pale blue with thin high cloud, brighter near the horizon. Exposed for his face, with readable shadows under the trees.

Tactile realism: rich blacks with readable colour, soft highlight roll-off, truthful skin colour, restrained fine grain over a sharp image. Texture comes from real surfaces and light, never a filter. Any signs or screens have no readable letters.

If any surface looks clean, plastic, grey, untextured or rendered, the image is wrong.
